content: In the study of stochastic processes, an adapted process, also referred to as a non-anticipating process, is one that does not have the ability to foresee future events. This concept is crucial, for example, in the definition of the Itō integral, which is only meaningful if the integrand is an adapted process. Definition Let us define the following components: ( (Omega, mathcal{F}, P) ): a probability space, where (Omega) is the sample space, (mathcal{F}) is the sigma-algebra, and (P) is the probability measure. (I): an index set equipped with a total order (leq). Common choices for (I) include (mathbb{N}) (natural numbers), (mathbb{N}_0) (non-negative integers), or ([0, +infty)) (non-negative real numbers). (mathcal{F}_= (mathcal{F}_i)_{i in I}): a filtration of the sigma-algebra (mathcal{F}), representing the evolution of information over time. ((S, Sigma)): a measurable space, referred to as the state space. (X: I times Omega to S): a stochastic process. The process (X) is said to be adapted to the filtration ((mathcal{F}_i)_{i in I}) if, for every (i in I), the random variable (X_i: Omega to S) is measurable with respect to ((mathcal{F}_i, Sigma)). In other words, the value of (X_i) depends only on the information available up to time (i), as encoded in (mathcal{F}_i). Examples Consider a stochastic process (X: I times Omega to mathbb{R}), where the real line (mathbb{R}) is equipped with its standard Borel sigma-algebra, which is generated by the open subsets of (mathbb{R}). 1. Adapted Process Example: If we take the natural filtration (mathcal{F}^X), where (mathcal{F}_t^X) is the sigma-algebra generated by the pre-images (X_s^{-1}(B)) for Borel subsets (B subseteq mathbb{R}) and times (0 leq s leq t), then the process (X) is automatically (mathcal{F}^X)-adapted. Intuitively, the natural filtration (mathcal{F}^X) contains all the information about the behavior of (X) up to time (t). 2. Non-Adapted Process Example: Let us define a filtration (mathcal{F}_t) as follows: For times (0 leq t < 1), (mathcal{F}_t) is the trivial sigma-algebra ({emptyset, Omega}), which contains no meaningful information. For times (1 leq t leq 2), (mathcal{F}_t = mathcal{F}_t^X), the natural filtration of (X). In this case, any process (X) that is non-constant on ([0, 1)) will fail to be (mathcal{F})-adapted. This is because a function can only be measurable with respect to the trivial sigma-algebra if it is constant. The non-constant nature of such a process (X) implies that it uses information from the more refined future sigma-algebras (mathcal{F}_t) for (1 leq t leq 2), which violates the definition of an adapted process.
